lines.text: Short arms don't lose fights.
Standing at his distance does.
Every tall fighter has one perfect distance.
Right at the end of his jab.
His punches land there. Yours fall short.
And that's exactly where you stand.
You wait there, looking for a gap.
He jabs. You reach. You miss.
Every second there costs you.
Mike Tyson was five foot ten.
He won the heavyweight title at twenty, against a man four inches taller.
He didn't hang around at the end of the jab.
Head moving, he'd slip, step, and arrive.
Up close, where long arms have no room to punch.
Getting inside is a skill you drill, the app I'm building trains you to do exactly that, and it starts with your head.
Don't walk in straight. Move your head as you step.
Cross the gap in one go. Never stop halfway.
Then stay close and work the body.
Be far, or be close.
Never in between.
